players.name: Claude Makélélé
players.note: The screen in front of a title-winning defence that conceded fifteen league goals; world class, a rung below Lampard (90) only because his contribution is the harder one to see.

players.name: John Terry
players.note: PFA Player of the Year in a title-winning side that conceded fifteen league goals. World class - reading, organisation and front-foot defending all at their peak, and the equal of the Ferdinand 2007/08 anchor.

players.name: Petr Čech
players.note: Fifteen goals conceded in 35 games and a record clean-sheet run. Positioning, handling and shot-stopping were all at the very top of the world game that season, which is what puts him in the 90s at 22 rather than the 80s.

players.name: Eiður Guðjohnsen
players.note: Twelve league goals in a title-winning side while spending much of the season dropping off the front to link play; a genuinely elite second striker.

players.name: Paulo Ferreira
players.note: A Champions League winner and Euro 2004 finalist starting at right back for the record-breaking Chelsea defence; positionally excellent, offensively limited.

players.name: William Gallas
players.note: Mostly at left-back in a title-winning side that conceded fifteen; elite as a defender, and better still for being able to do it anywhere across the back four.

players.name: Ricardo Carvalho
players.note: The reigning Champions League winner, and when fit the best defender in the record-breaking Chelsea back line — quick, aggressive in the tackle and a superb reader of a through ball.

players.name: Tiago Mendes
players.note: A title-winning central midfielder in a side that could pick anyone: energetic, tidy and a good runner into the box.

players.name: Joe Cole
players.note: Eight goals in nineteen starts as he began to add end product to the dribbling.

players.name: Didier Drogba
players.note: A title-winning centre-forward in his first English season: physically overwhelming and a real creator with his back to goal, but the finishing and decision-making were years from the player of 2009.

players.name: Arjen Robben
players.note: Injured for half of it and still, when on the pitch, the most dangerous attacking player in the title-winning side — seven goals and nine assists from 14 starts at 20.

players.name: Wayne Bridge
players.note: A broken ankle in February ended his season and cost him the left-back place for good.

players.name: Mateja Kežman
players.note: Four goals in a Chelsea title season reads as a failure, and it was - but this is a striker who scored a hundred goals in three Eredivisie seasons and went on scoring in Turkey and France. A sharp, one-dimensional finisher who did not fit.

players.name: Jiří Jarošík
players.note: A Czech international used all over the pitch by a title-winning side; genuinely versatile and technically sound without being good enough to start.
